title: Quantum Channel Capacities and Entanglement Assistance

items.title: Entropy bounds for a finite mixture of states
items.statement:
For states $\rho_i$ and finite probabilities $p_i$, put $\bar\rho=\sum_i p_i\rho_i$. Then
$$0\le S(\bar\rho)-\sum_i p_iS(\rho_i)\le H(p).$$
items.strategy: Finite-dimensional supplier-first proof; exact current carrier is authoritative.

items.title: Exponential averaged spectral projectors for a finite cq ensemble
items.statement:
For every fixed finite ensemble $p_x,\rho_x$ and fixed $\eta>0$, there are constants $C,c>0$ (depending on this ensemble and $\eta$, not $n$) and projectors $P_n,Q_{x^n}$ such that, writing $\bar\rho=\sum p_x\rho_x$ and $s=\sum p_xS(\rho_x)$,
$$\operatorname{rank}P_n\le e^{n(S(\bar\rho)+\eta)},\quad P_n\bar\rho^{\otimes n}P_n\preceq e^{-n(S(\bar\rho)-\eta)}P_n,$$
$$\operatorname{rank}Q_{x^n}\le e^{n(s+\eta)},\quad Q_{x^n}\rho_{x^n}Q_{x^n}\preceq e^{-n(s-\eta)}Q_{x^n},$$
and
$$\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{X^n}(I-P_n))\le Ce^{-cn},\qquad\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{X^n}(I-Q_{X^n}))\le Ce^{-cn}.$$
The second pair of algebraic bounds holds for every word, including words with zero sampling probability; no per-word high-acceptance assertion is required.
items.strategy: Finite-dimensional supplier-first proof; exact current carrier is authoritative.

items.title: Finite unitary averaging and a decoupling second-moment bound
items.statement:
Let $D\ge2$, $1\le K\le D$, and $\omega_{AE}\succeq0$ with $\dim A=D$, $\operatorname{tr}\omega\le1$, and $r=\operatorname{rank}\omega_E$. For every $\delta>0$ there is an explicitly specified finite probability ensemble of isometries $W:\mathbb C^K\to\mathbb C^D$ such that, for
$$\omega^W_{RE}=\frac DK(W^T\otimes I_E)\omega_{AE}(\overline W\otimes I_E),$$
one has
$$\mathbb E\left\|\omega^W_{RE}-\frac{I_R}{K}\otimes\omega_E\right\|_1\le\sqrt{2Kr\operatorname{tr}(\omega_{AE}^2)}+\delta.$$
At the same time the ensemble can be required to satisfy, for every Hermitian $Z_{AE}$,
$$\mathbb E\left\|\frac DK(W^T\otimes I)Z(\overline W\otimes I)\right\|_1\le(1+\delta)\|Z\|_1.$$
No Haar existence or Gaussian-law supplier, and no choice axiom, is used.
items.strategy: Finite-dimensional supplier-first proof; exact current carrier is authoritative.

items.title: Every finite extension is obtained from a purification by a channel
items.statement: Let $\omega_{ZA}$ be any finite-dimensional extension of $\rho_A$, and let $|\psi\rangle_{RA}$ purify $\rho_A$ with $R$ a copy of $A$. There is a CPTP map $\Lambda:R\to Z$ with $(\Lambda\otimes\operatorname{id}_A)(\psi)=\omega$.
items.strategy: Finite-dimensional supplier-first proof; exact current carrier is authoritative.

items.title: Finite-dimensional quantum erasure channel
items.statement: For a d-dimensional input and erasure probability ε∈[0,1], define the flagged erasure channel into the orthogonal sum of the data space and a one-dimensional erasure space.

items.title: Limit formula for linearly bounded superadditive sequences
items.statement: If a real sequence is superadditive and bounded in absolute value by a linear function, then a_n/n converges to sup_n a_n/n.

items.title: Complementary channels and coherent information
items.statement: Fix a finite Stinespring isometry for a finite-dimensional channel, define its complementary channel, and define coherent information through a purification with the convention I_c(ρ,N)=S(B)-S(RB).

items.title: Entropy of a finite flagged state
items.statement: For a finite state τ and a one-dimensional orthogonal flag, the entropy of pτ⊕(1−p)|e⟩⟨e| is h(p)+pS(τ), including p=0,1.

items.title: Data processing for finite quantum mutual information
items.statement: Applying local finite-dimensional quantum channels to the two registers cannot increase their quantum mutual information.

items.title: The maximally mixed state maximizes finite quantum entropy
items.statement: On a d-dimensional state space, S(ρ)≤ln d, with equality exactly for ρ=I/d.

items.title: Dimension-dependent quantum entropy continuity and Holevo control
items.statement: Write $h(t)=-t\ln t-(1-t)\ln(1-t)$ with continuous endpoints. Let $g(t)=(1+t)\ln(1+t)-t\ln t$ for $t\in[0,1]$, with $g(0)=0$. For states $\rho,\sigma$ on dimension $d\ge1$ and $t=\frac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1$, $$|S(\rho)-S(\sigma)|\le t\ln d+g(t).$$ Moreover, if $\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_M$ are states on that space and $a=M^{-1}\sum_m\frac12\|\sigma_m-\sigma\|_1$, their uniform Holevo information is at most $2a\ln d+2g(a)$. In particular on dimension $d_E^n$, exponential decay of $a$ makes unnormalized Holevo information tend to zero.
items.strategy: Finite-dimensional supplier-first proof; exact current carrier is authoritative.

items.title: Exact flat spectral-type reduction of channel information
items.statement: Let $\rho$ be a state on dimension $d$ and $\mathcal N$ a finite-dimensional channel. There is an exact decomposition $\rho^{\otimes n}=\sum_t p_t\tau_t$ into mutually orthogonal flat spectral-type states, with at most $(n+1)^d$ positive-weight types and $H(T)\le d\ln(n+1)$. For its fixed complementary channel, $$\sum_t p_t I_c(\tau_t,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})\ge nI_c(\rho,\mathcal N)-H(T),$$ $$\sum_t p_t[S(\tau_t)+I_c(\tau_t,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})]\ge n[S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)]-2H(T).$$ Thus in each inequality some flat type state attains at least the displayed lower bound.
items.strategy: Finite-dimensional supplier-first proof; exact current carrier is authoritative.

items.title: Flat-input coherent information is achievable by subspace codes
items.statement: Let $V:\mathbb C^d\to B\otimes E$ be a Stinespring isometry and $\tau=I_d/d$. Every $0<R<I_c(\tau,\mathcal N)$ is achievable by isometric subspace entanglement transmission. If the coherent information is nonpositive, the lower bound is supplied by the one-dimensional code. Here an $n$-use code has an isometry $W_n:\mathbb C^{K_n}\to A^{\otimes n}$ and a CPTP decoder to $\mathbb C^{K_n}$; its squared overlap with the maximally entangled target tends to one and $n^{-1}\ln K_n\to R$. The same conclusion holds for a flat state on any nonzero input subspace by composing with its embedding.
items.strategy: Finite-dimensional supplier-first proof; exact current carrier is authoritative.

items.title: The finite-dimensional erasure map is a quantum channel
items.statement: For each finite input dimension and erasure probability in [0,1], the flagged erasure map is completely positive and trace-preserving.

items.title: Degradable and antidegradable channels
items.statement: Define a channel as degradable when its complementary output is simulated from the receiver output, and antidegradable when the receiver output is simulated from the complementary output.

items.title: Coherent information equals output entropy minus environment entropy
items.statement: For every finite input state and every fixed Stinespring dilation, I_c(ρ,N)=S(N(ρ))-S(N^c(ρ)); hence this entropy difference is independent of the chosen purification and complementary dilation.

items.title: Private information of a finite channel ensemble
items.statement: For a finite ensemble of input states, define private information as the coherent information of its average input minus the average coherent information of the ensemble members.

items.title: Finite cq wiretap achievability with strong Holevo secrecy
items.statement: Fix any finite input ensemble $(p_x,\rho_x)$ for a finite-dimensional channel $\mathcal N$ and a complement $\mathcal N^c$. Let $\chi_B,\chi_E$ be the Holevo informations of their output ensembles. Every $0<R<\chi_B-\chi_E$ admits uniform $M_n$-message codes with mixed input states, Bob POVMs, $n^{-1}\ln M_n\to R$, average error tending to zero, and unnormalized complementary-output Holevo leakage tending to zero. The construction has exponentially decaying average error and average trace distance to a fixed complementary product target; dimension-dependent entropy control converts the latter to strong Holevo secrecy.
items.strategy: Finite-dimensional supplier-first proof; exact current carrier is authoritative.

items.title: Flat-input entanglement-assisted achievability by Weyl coding
items.statement: Let $\tau=JJ^*/D$ be the flat state of a nonzero $D$-dimensional input subspace of a finite-dimensional channel $\mathcal N$. With prior shared maximally entangled states on that subspace, every $0\le R<S(\tau)+I_c(\tau,\mathcal N)$ is achievable for classical messages with average error tending to zero. The code consists of finite Weyl operations followed by a collective output/reference POVM; it has rate tending to $R$.
items.strategy: Finite-dimensional supplier-first proof; exact current carrier is authoritative.

items.title: Finite channel information maxima are attained
items.statement: For every finite-dimensional channel, both ρ↦I_c(ρ,N) and ρ↦S(ρ)+I_c(ρ,N) attain maxima on the input state space.

items.title: Complement and degradation maps of the erasure channel
items.statement: The complementary erasure channel has erasure probability 1-ε; the channel is degradable for ε≤1/2 and antidegradable for ε≥1/2.

items.title: Private information is an average coherent-information difference
items.statement: For a finite input ensemble, private information equals I_c of the average input minus the ensemble average of I_c, and also equals the receiver Holevo quantity minus the environment Holevo quantity.

items.title: Product additivity of coherent and private information
items.statement: Coherent information is additive on product inputs and private information is additive on product ensembles for tensor-product channels.

items.title: Additivity of optimized entanglement-assisted information
items.statement: The maximum of S(ρ)+I_c(ρ,N), equivalently I(R;B) for a purification, is additive under tensor products of finite-dimensional channels.

items.title: Coherent information of a qudit erasure channel
items.statement: For every input state ρ, I_c(ρ,E_{d,ε})=(1−2ε)S(ρ), including ε=0 and ε=1.

items.title: Operational quantum, private, and entanglement-assisted capacities
items.statement: Define finite-block quantum transmission, strong-secrecy private classical transmission, and classical transmission with prior shared entanglement, and define their asymptotic rates in nats per channel use.

items.title: Coherent-information concavity and subadditivity for degradable channels
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional degradable channel, coherent information is concave, nonnegative, and additive across arbitrary correlated inputs to tensor products of degradable channels.

items.title: Regularized coherent-information formula for quantum capacity
items.statement: For every finite-dimensional memoryless quantum channel, its unassisted quantum capacity equals lim_n (1/n) sup_ρ I_c(ρ,N^⊗n), without asserting single-letter additivity in general.

items.title: Regularized private-information formula for quantum channel capacity
items.statement: For every finite-dimensional memoryless quantum channel, its strong-secrecy private classical capacity equals lim_n (1/n) sup_ensemble I_p(ensemble,N^⊗n), with no general single-letter claim.

items.title: Additive entanglement-assisted classical capacity formula
items.statement: For every finite-dimensional channel, C_E(N)=max_ρ[S(ρ)+I_c(ρ,N)]=max_ρ I(R;B), and C_E is additive under tensor products.

items.title: Single-letter quantum and private capacities of degradable channels
items.statement: For each finite-dimensional degradable channel, Q(N)=P(N)=max_ρ I_c(ρ,N), and tensor-power regularization is unnecessary.

items.title: Exact quantum, private, and entanglement-assisted erasure capacities
items.statement: For a d-dimensional erasure channel with probability ε, Q=P=max(1-2ε,0)ln d, and C_E=2(1-ε)ln d.

summary: Prove the finite-dimensional regularized coherent-information quantum-capacity formula and regularized private-information formula, the additive entanglement-assisted classical-capacity formula, the degradable-channel single-letter case, and exact qudit erasure-channel capacities. General unassisted quantum and private capacities remain regularized; no general single-letter additivity is asserted.

title: Quantum Channel Capacities and Entanglement Assistance — Examples

items.title: Entanglement-assisted capacity of a noiseless qubit
items.statement: The identity channel on a qubit has C_E=2 ln 2, achieved by dense coding with a shared Bell pair.

items.title: Capacity regimes of the qubit erasure channel
items.statement: For d=2 and representative erasure probabilities, compute Q, P, and C_E and identify degradable, self-complementary, and antidegradable regimes.

summary: Compute the noiseless dense-coding endpoint and qudit erasure-channel regimes from the A-page theorems, showing where degradability gives a single-letter answer and where the general capacity formulas remain regularized.
